# Receive-ZbxWatch

## SYNOPSIS

Reads the values a watch collects, as they arrive.

## SYNTAX

```
Receive-ZbxWatch [-Name] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Receive-ZbxWatch cmdlet writes each value the watch named in -Name collects, as a ZabbixValue with its host, key, value and clock, and keeps waiting for the next until the watch stops or the pipeline ends (Ctrl+C, or Select-Object -First). Each call is its own reader with a bounded buffer, so a slow reader loses the oldest values, which Get-ZbxWatch counts in Dropped. It sends nothing to the server itself; the watch does the reading.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Read the next value of a watched item

```powershell
Receive-ZbxWatch -Name 'items' | Select-Object -First 1 | Select-Object HostName, Key, Value
```

The reader sees the values that arrive after it starts; Select-Object -First ends it after one.

### Example 2: React to values as they arrive

```powershell
Receive-ZbxWatch -Name 'items' | Select-Object -First 3 |
    ForEach-Object { '{0} {1} = {2} at {3}' -f $_.HostName, $_.Key, $_.Value, $_.Time }
```

ForEach-Object handles each value as it comes: here it reports the time of the next three.
